title: n8n-io/n8n — Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities. Combine visual building with custom code, self-host or cloud, 400+ integrations.
content:
Fair-code platform to build and deploy AI agents and workflows. Combine a visual canvas with custom code, run it self-hosted or in the cloud, and connect to 1500+ integrations. AI automation you can trust with real work, from prototype to production.
- AI-Native Automation Platform: Build and operationalize AI workflows and multi-step agents using your own data, models, and tools
- Model Flexibility, No Lock-In: Connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or open-source models and switch providers without changing your architecture
- From Prototype to Production: Design multi-step AI workflows with logic, tool use, human approvals, and full observability
- Code When You Need It: Combine visual building with JavaScript, Python, and npm packages for advanced AI workflows
- Enterprise-Ready AI: Self-host or deploy securely with role-based access, audit trails, and support for sensitive data
- Leverage What Already Exists: 1500+ integrations and 9,000+ workflow templates to connect AI with your existing systems
Try n8n instantly with our install script (requires Docker):
curl -fsSL https://get.n8n.io | sh
Or deploy manually with Docker:
docker volume create n8n_data
docker run -it --rm --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n
Access the editor at http://localhost:5678

Short answer: It means "nodemation" and is pronounced as n-eight-n.
Long answer: "I get that question quite often (more often than I expected) so I decided it is probably best to answer it here. While looking for a good name for the project with a free domain I realized very quickly that all the good ones I could think of were already taken. So, in the end, I chose nodemation. 'node-' in the sense that it uses a Node-View and that it uses Node.js and '-mation' for 'automation' which is what the project is supposed to help with. However, I did not like how long the name was and I could not imagine writing something that long every time in the CLI. That is when I then ended up on 'n8n'." - Jan Oberhauser, Founder and CEO, n8n.io

report.summary: n8n is a fair-code, AI-native workflow automation platform that combines visual building and custom code for self-hosted or cloud deployment.
report.background: Workflow automation tools like Zapier and Make popularized connecting apps without code. As AI agents moved from demos to production, teams needed automation platforms that support LLMs, custom code, data privacy, and self-hosting. n8n emerged as a fair-code alternative: source-available, extensible, and deployable anywhere. It integrates LangChain-style AI workflows, letting users build multi-step agents with their own models and tools. The rise of open-source and commercial LLMs also increased demand for model flexibility and no vendor lock-in. n8n addresses this by combining a visual canvas, 1500+ integrations, and enterprise features, positioning itself between no-code automation and developer-first orchestration for AI workflows.
key_points: AI-native workflows and agents: n8n lets users build multi-step AI agents using their own data, models, and tools, connecting to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or open-source LLMs without changing architecture.
Visual building plus custom code: users can design automations on a canvas, then add JavaScript, Python, and npm packages when advanced logic or custom AI steps are needed.
Large integration and template ecosystem: n8n offers 1500+ integrations and 9000+ workflow templates, helping teams connect AI to existing systems quickly instead of starting from scratch.
Self-host or cloud with enterprise controls: it supports Docker-based self-hosting or secure cloud deployment, with role-based access, audit trails, and support for sensitive data.
Fair-code licensing: n8n is source-available under the Sustainable Use License and Enterprise License, allowing self-hosting and extensibility while offering paid enterprise features and support.
report.impact: For the AI industry, n8n strengthens the shift from closed automation suites to flexible, AI-native orchestration that can run anywhere. Developers gain a production-ready way to combine LLMs, APIs, and custom code without rebuilding infrastructure. Regular users benefit from accessible templates and a visual editor, making AI automation less intimidating. Because n8n supports self-hosting and multiple model providers, it reduces vendor lock-in and helps companies keep sensitive data in-house. It also increases competition with Zapier, Make, and newer agent frameworks, pushing the market toward open, extensible, and privacy-conscious automation. Teams can prototype quickly, then scale workflows into reliable production systems with observability and approvals.
report.tools: Follow n8n's official docs, AI and LangChain guide, integration library, and example workflows. For alternatives or complements, watch LangChain, Flowise, Dify, Activepieces, AutoGen, and CrewAI. To try n8n, use Docker or the install script, then explore community templates and the forum for production patterns.
